name: חַוָּה
gloss: life, living; mother of all living
summary: The first woman, made from the man's side and brought to him (Gen 2:21–22), Adam's wife and the mother of Cain, Abel and Seth (Gen 4:1–2, 25). After the judgment in the garden “the man called his wife's name חַוָּה, because she was the mother of all living (כָּל־חָי)” (Gen 3:20): scripture itself ties the name to חַי “living”. The form keeps the w of the root (ḥwy), which Hebrew חָיָה has lost but Ugaritic, Phoenician and Sabaic keep, and which shows also in Aramaic חֵיוָא “beast”. Paul names her twice: the serpent deceived Eve by its craftiness (2Co 11:3), and Adam was formed first, then Eve (1Ti 2:13).

evidence.note: “The man called the name of his wife חַוָּה, for she was אֵם כָּל־חָי, the mother of all living.”
Yahweh God built the rib he had taken from the man into a woman and brought her to the man.
The woman's seed, given before she is named for the life she will bear.
“The man knew חַוָּה his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain.”
She bore Seth, “another seed instead of Abel”.
“As the serpent deceived Eve by its craftiness.”

note: BDB files חַוָּה under חוה with “declare” and “tent-village”; the entry is attached to חיה because Gen 3:20 explains the name by כָּל־חָי and because the root ḥwy “live” is attested with w in Ugaritic (Segert p. 185), Phoenician (Krahmalkov pp. 178–179) and Sabaic (Biella pp. 168–169, which itself compares the Hebrew name). Whoever drafts חוה should not claim h.ba.ab. The reading of the name as “serpent” (Aramaic חִוְיָא, Arabic ḥayyah) is a lead from later sources that Gen 3:20 does not support; not entered. The Septuagint at Gen 3:20 translates the name Ζωή; the New Testament spells it Εὕα.
